evidence.observation: Dashboard component makes 3 concurrent API calls on mount with no error handling. When access token is missing/expired, all 3 requests trigger 401 responses and attempt concurrent refresh.
api() calls refreshSession() when receiving 401. If refreshSession() returns false, logout() is called, redirecting to login page without error message to user.
refreshSession() returns false if POST /auth/refresh does not return ok status. Multiple concurrent calls to this function will all attempt to use the same refresh token.

Token rotation revokes the old token (line 60) and then awaits async calls (lines 61-62). The await yields the event loop, creating a window where a concurrent request can find the same token marked revoked and call revokeFamily().
refreshController catches TokenReuseDetected and returns 401 with cleared cookie. A concurrent refresh that triggers this loses its cookie and the user is immediately logged out.
Token revocation sets revoked_at timestamp in database. Called at line 60 of tokenService.ts before the async yield.
logout() performs synchronous navigation to /login. No error message is shown to user before navigation — this explains the 'silent' logout.
Access token is stored in module-level variable. Cleared on page reload, causing api() calls to omit Authorization header.

authMiddleware returns 401 if Authorization header is missing or if the token's family is revoked. If a family was revoked during concurrent refresh, even newly-issued tokens with that family ID will be rejected.
Access token TTL is 900 seconds (15 minutes). Users away longer than this will have expired tokens and trigger a 401 + refresh flow on next request.
/auth/refresh endpoint is unprotected. Protected routes require Authorization header. On page reload with no in-memory token, all protected route requests fail with 401 simultaneously.

hypotheses.statement: Users experience silent logout due to concurrent token refresh calls triggered by the 3 parallel API requests in Dashboard.useEffect — the second and third refresh requests detect 'token reuse' and revoke the family.
On page reload, _accessToken is cleared, causing all initial API requests to omit Authorization header and receive 401.

When the first concurrent refresh attempt succeeds, it marks the refresh token as revoked. Concurrent refresh attempts with the same token detect revocation and throw TokenReuseDetected, revoking the entire family.
Even if the first refresh succeeds and returns new tokens, the family may already be revoked by a concurrent request, causing authMiddleware to reject the new access token with 401.
The 15-minute access token TTL is short enough that users returning after a moderate absence will always have an expired token, reliably triggering the concurrent refresh race.
